purpose: Preserve durable, evidence-backed project decisions, technical debt, and experiments so future sessions can reason from current project history instead of stale conversational memory.

reviewRules: Every material product, revenue, payment, legal, security, architecture, scope, or operating-model decision should have a durable record once approved.
A prior approved decision may be reopened only when new evidence, a review trigger, or an explicit owner request exists.
Superseding a decision requires a new decision record that references the prior decision ID.
Record deliberate shortcuts, known design limitations, missing tests, migration remnants, unsafe temporary assumptions, or maintainability liabilities that remain after a task.
Do not record ordinary backlog ideas as technical debt unless there is a concrete existing liability.
A debt item may be marked resolved only with resolution evidence.
Use an experiment when an important product, revenue, support, or growth choice is uncertain and can be validated with a bounded test.
Define the hypothesis, primary metric, evidence source, decision rule, guardrails, audience, and stop condition before execution.
Do not fabricate a baseline, target, result, conversion rate, or market metric. Unknown values must remain explicitly unknown until measured.
A completed experiment requires evidence and a conclusion of keep, iterate, stop, or inconclusive.

reviewCadence: at the start of every substantial new coordinator session
before a material product, revenue, payment, architecture, legal, security, or launch decision
at the end of every major milestone
when repeated learning or performance signals may be explained by an old decision, recurring debt, or a failed experiment
